correctness.rationale: In a unicyclic graph every spanning tree deletes one uniformly random cycle edge J, so degree of cycle vertex u is deg_G(u)−I(J incident u); the two incidence probabilities 2/ℓ and overlap probability 1/ℓ only for adjacent cycle vertices give (ℓ−4)/ℓ² and −4/ℓ², with off-cycle degrees deterministic. For n≤5 enumerate all 2^{n choose 2} labeled graphs, filter connected, enumerate every (n−1)-edge tree and each pair covariance via integer NΣD_uD_v−(ΣD_u)(ΣD_v), then canonicalize via all n! label permutations. Independent recreation yields connected labeled graph counts 1,4,38,728 and class counts 1,2,6,21, exactly two positive classes at n5, with witnesses 5 spanning trees and 1/25, or 11 trees and 5/121. This is a complete finite classification backed by exhaustive cases; the all-order unicyclic statement is separately analytic.

value.rationale: A sharp minimal counterexample to extending edge negative dependence to vertex-degree covariance is a natural graph invariant. A complete five-vertex isomorphism classification plus the all-order cycle-length phase transition is useful and mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary small-case recomputation.

final_claim: For uniform spanning trees of connected simple graphs, positive covariance of two distinct vertex degrees is impossible at n≤4; at n=5 exactly the C5 and C5-plus-chord isomorphism types have positive pairs (respectively 5 pairs of covariance 1/25, 2 pairs of covariance 5/121); all unicyclic graphs admit the given (ℓ−4)/ℓ², −4/ℓ², 0 covariance trichotomy.
limitations: No complete classification at n≥6, no weighted/uniform-minimum spanning tree extension.
